name: mcptoolcheck
one_liner: Static linter for MCP tool-descriptor files (tools/list snapshots, server-side manifests, generic tool-advertise JSON) - flags twelve shape defects that enable approval-view fidelity gaps and silent descriptor drift.
problem: The MCP tool-advertisement surface - the name / description / inputSchema / annotations each server exposes via its tools/list handshake - is a trust boundary between the server operator and the agent host, and the host must decide (once, in an approval dialog) whether to trust the surface. Two converging 2026 signals establish a current unmet need on that surface. arXiv 2607.05744 (Rashidi, 2026-07-07, 'Unicode TAG-Block Concealment of Tool-Metadata Payloads in the Model Context Protocol: An Approval-View Fidelity Gap Across Three Independent Server Implementations') shows that Plane 14 TAG characters (U+E0000-U+E007F), bidi overrides, zero-width characters, and private-use codepoints are invisible in approval dialogs but reach the model tokenizer, and that 8/8 attack techniques evade a human reviewer across three independent server implementations. The 2026-10-04 field report at github.com/Paraphern/rugsnare catalogues 140 silent changes across 66 release pairs of four reference MCP servers - 43 BREAKING schema flips, 28 annotation flips (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint), 7 cosmetic rewordings - 'not one was announced in a changelog.' mcptoolcheck reads a tools/list snapshot, server-side manifest, or any JSON blob with tool-advertisement objects and flags twelve shape defects across invisible-character concealment, cross-script homoglyph spoofing, name-field hygiene, missing version / hash pin (silent-change detection surface), annotation-flip inconsistency (readOnlyHint on a 'delete/write/update'-named tool, destructiveHint on a 'read/list/get'-named tool), missing annotations, permissive or absent inputSchema, and length anomalies. This is an independent implementation, not affiliated with or endorsed by the authors of the paper or of the field report.
clean_room: Rules are derived from the public abstract of arXiv 2607.05744 (named concealment classes: Plane 14 Tags, bidi overrides, zero-width, control, private-use; the five metadata surfaces listed in the paper), from the public README of github.com/Paraphern/rugsnare (named silent-change categories: BREAKING schema flips, ANNOTATION flips, COSMETIC rewordings; the four pinnable surfaces named by the field report: name, description, inputSchema, readOnlyHint / destructiveHint), and from the public Model Context Protocol JSON-RPC specification for tools/list response shape. No reference implementation of either artifact (the paper's companion code, if any, or rugsnare's gateway source) was read, vendored, or mirrored. The paper's rung-1 pattern-recognition surface is intentionally exposed by these rules; rung-2 interventional-closure arguments are out of scope for a shape-only linter.
